deep.reconstruction:
The page has two unrelated pieces of work, separated by a horizontal rule.

(A) TOP: an n x n array with prescribed row and column sums.
- Unknowns y_{α,β} ≥ 0, with row sums Σ_β y_{α,β} = s_α and column sums Σ_α y_{α,β} = t_β.
- Total p = Σ_α s_α = Σ_β t_β. This is implicit; the line y_{1,1} = p − t_2 − … − t_n − … shows it.
- Riemann writes out the rows: y_{1,1}+y_{1,2}+…+y_{1,n} = s_1, …, y_{n,1}+…+y_{n,n} = s_n.
- He takes the inner (n−1)×(n−1) block (α, β ≥ 2) as free parameters. The first column and first row are then
  y_{α,1} = s_α − Σ_{β≥2} y_{α,β}  and  y_{1,β} = t_β − Σ_{α≥2} y_{α,β}.
- The corner entry follows (filled step mine): y_{1,1} = s_1 − Σ_{β≥2} y_{1,β} = s_1 − Σ_{β≥2} t_β + Σ_{α,β≥2} y_{α,β}. Using s_1 = p − Σ_{α≥2} s_α:
  y_{1,1} = p − Σ_{β≥2} t_β − Σ_{α≥2} s_α + Σ_{α,β≥2} y_{α,β}.
- Nonnegativity of the eliminated entries gives the constraints he writes:
  - y_{α,1} ≥ 0 ⇔ Σ_β y_{α,β} ≤ s_α (he writes <);
  - y_{1,β} ≥ 0 ⇔ Σ_α y_{α,β} ≤ t_β;
  - y_{1,1} ≥ 0 ⇔ Σ_{α,β≥2} y_{α,β} ≥ Σ_{β≥2} t_β + Σ_{α≥2} s_α − p.
- In modern terms this is the standard parametrisation of a transportation polytope (contingency tables with fixed margins), of dimension (n−1)². The application is not stated; it may be counting or probability, or tied to the nested-rectangle sketches at right. Those sketches appear to show nested rectangles/squares with interior dots, purpose unclear.

(B) BOTTOM: free-edge conditions for a rectangular elastic plate |x| ≤ a, |y| ≤ b (Kirchhoff plate, θ = Kirchhoff's elastic constant).
- Write ν = θ/(1+2θ), so 1−ν = (1+θ)/(1+2θ).
- Strain energy (my reconstruction from the coefficients) is ∝ ∫∫ [ ν (Δw)² + (1−ν)(w_xx² + w_yy² + 2 w_xy²) ] dx dy.
- Riemann writes the boundary terms of the first variation on an edge x = const. The coefficient written in front of each line multiplies the whole line.
  - Line 1, from ν(Δw)²: ν[ ∫ dy Δw δw_x − ∫ dy (w_xxx + w_xyy) δw ].
  - Line 2, from (1−ν)(w_xx² + 2w_xy² + …): (1−ν)[ ∫ dy w_xx δw_x − ∫ dy w_xxx δw + 2∫ dy w_xy δw_y ].
  - The last term is struck out and replaced, after integrating by parts in y, by −2∫ dy w_xyy δw plus the endpoint term +2 w_xy δw at x = ±a, y = ±b.
- Collecting the coefficient of δw_x gives the vanishing bending moment:
  w_xx + (θ/(1+2θ)) w_yy = 0.
- Collecting the coefficient of δw gives the Kirchhoff effective shear:
  ν(w_xxx + w_xyy) + (1−ν)(w_xxx + 2w_xyy) = w_xxx + (2−ν) w_xyy = 0, with 2−ν = (2+3θ)/(1+2θ).
  This is exactly Riemann's w_xxx + (2+3θ)/(1+2θ) w_xyy = 0.
- The leftover endpoint term 2(1−ν) w_xy δw gives the corner condition w_xy = 0 at x = ±a, y = ±b.
- These are Kirchhoff's (1850) free-edge conditions for the square/rectangular plate, i.e. the Chladni-figure problem. The biharmonic field equation is not written on this page.
errors: Row/column constraints are written with strict '<' where '≤' (nonnegativity) is meant.

In the plate variation the factors θ/(1+2θ) and (1+θ)/(1+2θ) are written only in front of the first integral of each line. They must be read as multiplying the whole line; otherwise the stated δw-coefficient (2+3θ)/(1+2θ) would not follow. Read that way, the result is correct.
The transposed index ranges (Σ over α, β from 2 to n) are only partly indicated (e.g. 'Σ_2'). The top derivation is correct with those ranges.

results.what: Parametrisation of n×n nonnegative arrays with given row sums s_α and column sums t_β by the inner (n−1)² entries, with the inequality constraints
results.modern_name: transportation polytope / contingency tables with fixed margins

results.what: Free-edge boundary conditions of a rectangular Kirchhoff plate derived from the energy variation: w_xx+ν w_yy=0, w_xxx+(2−ν)w_xyy=0 with ν=θ/(1+2θ), and corner condition w_xy=0
results.modern_name: Kirchhoff free-edge conditions (bending moment and effective shear) with corner forces
results.usually_credited_to: G. Kirchhoff 1850 (Crelle 40); corner-force interpretation Thomson & Tait 1867

deep.surprise_reason: Both computations are correct but standard. The plate part reproduces Kirchhoff's 1850 free-edge conditions in Kirchhoff's own θ-notation, so it is evidently Riemann studying Kirchhoff's paper. Its explicit corner condition is a mildly interesting unpublished detail, not a new result.

checkable.asserts: the two line coefficients are ν and 1−ν
combined δw_x coefficient: ν(w_xx+w_yy)+(1−ν)w_xx = w_xx+ν w_yy (C=w_xx, D=w_yy)

checkable.sympy: y=Matrix(3,3,lambda i,j: Symbol('y%d%d'%(i+1,j+1))); s=[sum(y.row(i)) for i in range(3)]; t=[sum(y.col(j)) for j in range(3)]; p=sum(s); simplify(y[0,0] - (p - t[1]-t[2] - s[1]-s[2] + y[1,1]+y[1,2]+y[2,1]+y[2,2])) == 0

transcription_corrections: The coefficients θ/(1+2θ) and (1+θ)/(1+2θ) in the left margin of the two variation lines govern the entire line, not just the first integral.
'Σ_2 y_{α,β}' should be read as Σ_{β=2}^{n} y_{α,β}, and the sums in the y_{1,1} formula run over α, β ≥ 2.
The relation between Σ_{α,β} y_{α,β} and Σ_β t_β+Σ_α s_α−p has an overwritten symbol. Mathematically it must be '≥' (the condition y_{1,1} ≥ 0).
'y_{1,n}=s_1', 'y_{2,n}=s_2', 'y_{n,n}=s_n' are the ends of full row sums y_{α,1}+y_{α,2}+…+y_{α,n}=s_α; the third row label is y_{n,1}+y_{n,2}+…
Final line: corner condition ∂²w/∂x∂y=0 at x=±a, y=±b, arising from the endpoint term +2 ∂²w/∂x∂y δw.
